dual-energy CT can provide a set of images for routine diagnostic image interpretation that are of improved quality relative to 120-kV scans for adult patients and of comparable quality for pediatric patients.
the quality of linearly combined dual-energy CT images is similar to or better than that of 120 kV CT images for the purpose for routine diagnostic interpretation.

dual-energy mixed images can provide single-energy-like images for a wide range of adult patient sizes and can provide images that are of similar quality or improved quality relative 120 kV single-energy scans.

the optimization and evaluation of image quality of linear mixed images in dual-energy CT.
the optimization and evaluation of the image quality of dual-source, dualenergy CT images for routine diagnostic use.
image quality optimization and evaluation in dual-source, linearly mixed images.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the linear mixed images are not of the same quality as 120 kV single-energy scans.
the image quality of the linear mixed images is comparable to the image quality of 120 kV single-energy CT images.
dual-energy CT can provide both material-specific and non-material-specific images with similar or improved quality compared to single-energy 80 or 120 kV CT for the same radiation exposure.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the use of dual-source, dualenergy CT for the purpose for material-specific imaging can be a viable approach to provide both material-specific and non-material-specific images at similar or improved image quality and at a similar radiation dose relative to single-energy CT.
dual-energy CT may provide a means to achieve material-specific information while maintaining a single set of routine diagnostic quality images.
dual-energy CT can be used for material-specific imaging and also for non-material-specific imaging.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the linear combination of low- and high energy images can produce images with similar noise and similar to improved CNR relative to conventional single energy 120 kV imaging.
dual-energy mixed images may be a viable alternative to conventional single-energy CT for the routine diagnostic interpretation of CT examinations.

, for adult patients, the quality of dual-energy mixed images is similar or improved relative to single-energy images acquired for the same total radiation, and that dual-energy CT can provide a set of nonmaterial specific images that are of diagnostic quality and can replace the use of single-energy CT.
